decisions.reason: Clarifying that the module has 40 pins rather than the development board's 44 duplicated pins does not change any established GPIO assignment.
The module pin-count clarification does not alter the board dimensions, component placement, connector placement, orientation, or enclosure-fit rules.
The 40-versus-44 count concerns ESP32 module and development-board pins, not the main board's JST or USB connector inventory.
The ESP32 module pin-count clarification does not change the monitored rails, monitor IC, channel count, or current-monitor placement.
The clarification does not change the addressable LED supply voltage, power switching, or ESP32 data-level handling.
The module pin count does not affect the standalone USB power source, activation condition, LDO capacity, or powered scope.
The source distinguishes ESP32 development-board pins from module pins and does not modify any sensor-board connector, pinout, or connector count.
The ESP32 module pin-count clarification does not alter the charge-status indicator, GPIO13 assignment, connector, or resistor configuration.
The source does not change the sensor board's mounting orientation, component arrangement, or interboard connector alignment.
The distinction between development-board and module pin counts does not change the requirement for local decoupling capacitors.
The module pin-count clarification does not modify panel-control presence, connector mode, GPIO mappings, reset wiring, or BOOT-button placement.
The source does not affect the power sources, Schottky OR-ing method, diode requirement, or source-selection behavior.
